Zaporizhya New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zaporizka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Zaporizhya — known as Aleksandrovsk until 1921 — had 22,631 Jews by 1939, among the larger Jewish populations documented in this collection. About 4,000 remained when the city was occupied in October 1941, most of whom were murdered that March. The community re-emerged after the war, with a synagogue reopened in 1947 and, following the 1990s revival, several Jewish cultural and educational organizations active today; a new synagogue was inaugurated in 2012. This cemetery's one surviving matzevah, dated 1930, bears a Russian inscription for Daniil Abramovich Usherovich.
